# splunk_config.yml settings

Generated from the Pydantic schema and `examples/catalog/features.yml`.
Do not edit this file; regenerate with
`spa --no-agent config schema --markdown`.
Concise lookup is `spa config search QUERY`, then `spa config explain PATH`.
CLI flags stay in [commands.md](commands.md).

| Path | Type | Qualifiers | Description |

### Snippets

#### Inventory plugin name

`plugin`

First line of every splunk_config.yml. It tells Ansible to load SPA's inventory plugin. spa init writes this; do not change it.

```yaml
plugin: splunk-platform-automator
```

## General

| Path | Type | Qualifiers | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `general` | object | optional | Settings for the lab index page written after deploy. Holds no value itself. |
| `general.url_locale` | string | optional; default='en-GB'; pattern=^[a-z]{2}[_-][A-Z]{2}$ | Language segment in the Splunk Web links on the lab index page, such as en-GB. |
| `custom` | CustomConfig | optional | Ansible connection variables for hosts SPA did not provision, such as ansible_user and ansible_port. No default. Omit the block when SPA provisions the hosts. |

### Snippets

#### Locale of the generated host-link page

`general`

After deploy, SPA writes $SPA_ENV_DIR/config/index.html with buttons into Splunk Web on each host. url_locale is the language path in those URLs (en-US, en-GB). Pattern is two lowercase letters, hyphen or underscore, two uppercase letters. Default in the template is en-GB if unset.

```yaml
general:
  url_locale: en-US
```

#### Custom Ansible connection vars

`custom`

Bring-your-own hosts (SSH already works; SPA did not provision them). Sets ansible_user, ansible_port, ansible_ssh_private_key_file, and similar connection variables for the inventory. Per-host custom: under splunk_hosts[].custom. Not a substitute for terraform.aws.ssh_username on AWS-provisioned labs.

```yaml
custom:
  ansible_user: ansible
  ansible_port: 22
  ansible_ssh_private_key_file: ~/.ssh/ansible_id_rsa
```

## OS

| Path | Type | Qualifiers | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `os` | object | optional | Guest OS settings applied before Splunk is installed. Holds no value itself. |
| `os.disable_apparmor` | boolean | optional; default=True | When true, disable AppArmor on Ubuntu and Debian. |
| `os.disable_selinux` | boolean | optional; default=True | When true, disable SELinux on RHEL and Amazon Linux. Skipped on universal forwarders. |
| `os.enable_time_sync_cron` | boolean | optional; default=False | When true, install a cron job that keeps the guest clock in sync. VirtualBox always turns this on. |
| `os.packages` | list[string] | optional; default=[] | Extra packages installed with the guest package manager before Splunk. acl is required (Ansible become fails without setfacl). polkit on RHEL and Amazon Linux, or policykit-1 on Ubuntu and Debian, is required unless splunk_use_policykit is false. |
| `os.remote_command` | string | optional | Shell command run on the guest before Ansible bootstraps, for an image that lacks Python or acl. No default. Omit the key to skip it. |
| `os.set_hostname` | boolean | optional; default=False | When true, set the guest hostname to its inventory name. |
| `os.splunk_group_create` | boolean | optional; default=True | When true, create the Splunk OS group. Set false when the group already exists on the image or comes from a directory service. |
| `os.splunk_user_create` | boolean | optional; default=True | When true, create the Splunk OS user. Set false when the account already exists; SPA then only uses it. |
| `os.ssh_keys` | list[string] | optional; default=[] | Public key files on the Ansible controller, appended to the login user's authorized_keys. Existing authorized_keys entries are kept. Apply on its own with spa run ssh_keys. |
| `os.time_zone` | string | optional | IANA time zone set on the guest. Default is the Ansible controller's zone. Omit the key to keep that. |
| `os.update_hosts_file` | boolean | optional; default=True | When true, write every lab host into /etc/hosts. Apply on its own with spa run update_hosts_file. |

### Snippets

#### Guest OS prerequisites, hardening, and access

`os`

Everything the Linux guest needs before Splunk installs, applied by the common role: extra packages (acl and polkit/policykit-1 are prerequisites), hostname, time zone and time-sync cron, SELinux/AppArmor, /etc/hosts entries for the env, operator SSH keys in authorized_keys, a pre-Ansible bootstrap command, and whether SPA creates the splunk user and group. Write it after init and pair the values with the AMI or box you chose; OS settings are deliberately not part of the topology or provider files.

```yaml
os:
  set_hostname: true
  packages: [acl, polkit]
  disable_selinux: true
```

#### Ubuntu / Debian OS block

`os.disable_apparmor`

Ubuntu LTS or Debian guests: the policykit package is policykit-1 (not polkit) and the MAC layer to disable is AppArmor (not SELinux). Otherwise the same keys as os.

```yaml
os:
  set_hostname: true
  disable_apparmor: true
  packages: [acl, policykit-1]
```

### Snippets

#### SSH username for AWS

`terraform.aws.ssh_username`

Login user Terraform and Ansible use on the EC2 AMI. Must match the image (ec2-user on Amazon Linux and RHEL, ubuntu on Ubuntu, admin on Debian). Discover with spa aws --describe-ami / --latest-ami. Always set it explicitly for AWS labs.

```yaml
terraform:
  aws:
    ssh_username: ec2-user
```

### Snippets

#### Indexer cluster factors

`splunk_idxclusters[].idxc_name`

Declares each indexer cluster that hosts reference with idxcluster. idxc_name is the id. idxc_rf / idxc_sf are single-site replication and search factors (lab usually 2; sf must not exceed rf or peer count). Multisite uses idxc_site_rf / idxc_site_sf instead, as Splunk factor strings such as origin:2, total:3. idxc_replication_port is the cluster replication port. Passwords are shared secrets; use lookups.

```yaml
splunk_idxclusters:
  - idxc_name: idxc1
    idxc_rf: 2
    idxc_sf: 2
```

#### Search head cluster

`splunk_shclusters[].shc_name`

Declares each search head cluster that deployers and search heads reference with shcluster. shc_name is the id. shc_site is siteN when search heads are site-aware. shc_replication_port is the SHC replication port (lab examples use 9887). shc_password is the shared secret; use a lookup.

```yaml
splunk_shclusters:
  - shc_name: shc1
    shc_password: "{{ lookup('env', 'SPLUNK_SHC_PASSWORD') }}"
    shc_replication_port: 9887
```

### Snippets

#### splunk_defaults section

`splunk_defaults`

Parent map for environment-wide Splunk settings (version, licenses, SSL, indexes, and the other keys under splunk_defaults). spa init may write an empty or minimal block; add keys by merging specific catalog snippets rather than copying this empty one.

```yaml
splunk_defaults: {}
```

#### Splunk admin password

`splunk_defaults.splunk_admin_password`

Password for the Splunk admin user created at install. Required under splunk_defaults. A literal password is valid. Prefer an env or vault lookup. Override per host or per named environment when stacks must not share the password.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_admin_password: "{{ lookup('env', 'SPLUNK_ADMIN_PASSWORD') }}"
```

#### Splunk installer architecture

`splunk_defaults.splunk_architecture`

CPU suffix of the Splunk tarball (amd64, x86_64, or arm64), not the architecture of the machine running spa. VirtualBox AlmaLinux labs are amd64 even on Apple Silicon hosts.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_architecture: amd64
```

#### Extra Splunk .conf stanzas

`splunk_defaults.splunk_conf`

Escape hatch for settings that have no dedicated SPA key. Map is path-under-etc -> stanza -> key: value, written into that conf file (often via a generated app). Prefer a catalog setting when one exists (indexes, SSL, volumes). Per-host splunk_hosts[].splunk_conf merges over the defaults.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_conf:
    system/local/limits.conf:
      diskUsage:
        minFreeSpace: 500
```

#### Download Splunk archives from splunk.com

`splunk_defaults.splunk_download`

Optional fetch of the Enterprise or Universal Forwarder tarball into Software during deploy. You still need the archive (or a prior download) in the Software directory because the installer license agreement is accepted from that file. Incomplete (#65).

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_download:
    splunk: true
    splunkforwarder: true
```

#### Splunk environment name

`splunk_defaults.splunk_env_name`

Short name for this Splunk stack (default splk). Used in inventory grouping and app naming. When splunk_environments lists more than one stack in one config, each host sets splunk_hosts[].splunk_env to one of those names.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_env_name: splk
```

#### Splunk FIPS mode

`splunk_defaults.splunk_fips`

Turns on Splunk Enterprise FIPS at install when the lab must use FIPS-validated crypto. Needs a FIPS-capable installer and matching OS packages; not a substitute for OS-level FIPS.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_fips: true
```

#### Indexer volumes

`splunk_defaults.splunk_indexer_volumes`

Named indexes.conf volumes (hot/cold paths on disk) and size limits. Each volume needs a filesystem path that already exists or that you create outside SPA. maxVolumeDataSizeMB on a volume overrides VolumeDataSize_Free_MB. homePath and coldPath name which volume default indexes use when splunk_indexes_default_paths is true.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_indexer_volumes:
    primary:
      path: /splunkdata/hot
      maxVolumeDataSizeMB: 50000
    cold:
      path: /splunkdata/cold
  splunk_volume_defaults:
    VolumeDataSize_Free_MB: 5000
    homePath: primary
    coldPath: cold
```

#### SmartStore remote volume

`splunk_defaults.splunk_indexer_volumes.<volume>.storageType`

Indexer SmartStore (S2): a named volume whose path is an s3:// bucket/prefix with storageType remote, and splunk_volume_defaults.remotePath pointing at that volume. homePath and coldPath must be the same volume when SmartStore is on. SPA does not create the bucket or IAM role; the operator owns those. Optional remote.s3.tsidx_compression on Splunk 9.0+. Start from separate indexer and search-head hosts, or a multisite indexer cluster with a search head cluster, then merge this snippet; do not copy leftover mixed SmartStore example files.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_indexer_volumes:
    hot:
    s2volume:
      path: s3://YOUR_BUCKET/prefix
      storageType: remote
  splunk_volume_defaults:
    homePath: hot
    coldPath: hot
    remotePath: s2volume
```

#### Index definitions

`splunk_defaults.splunk_indexes`

Creates indexes.conf indexes on indexers. Map key is the index name. Nested keys are indexes.conf settings (frozenTimePeriodInSecs, datatype, and so on). datatype metric makes a metrics index. splunk_indexes_default_paths true (default) lets SPA fill homePath/coldPath from volume defaults; set false only when you set those paths yourself.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_indexes:
    test1:
      frozenTimePeriodInSecs: 604800
    test2_metrics:
      datatype: metric
```

#### WiredTiger KV store engine

`splunk_defaults.splunk_kv_store_engine_wiredtiger`

Splunk 8.1+ can run KV Store on WiredTiger instead of MMAPv1. Set true when you want that engine on Enterprise hosts that support it. Leave unset to keep Splunk's default for the installed version.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_kv_store_engine_wiredtiger: true
```

#### License file and license server

`splunk_defaults.splunk_license_server`

Copy .lic files from Software onto a host with role license_manager, or point other hosts at an existing license manager with splunk_license_server (IP or FQDN). Pairing is checked by spa validate and spa licenses. ITSI/ES need matching entitlement files.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_license_file: Splunk_Enterprise.lic
```

#### Splunk Web login-screen hints

`splunk_defaults.splunk_loginpage_print_hostname`

Extra HTML on the Splunk Web login screen (web.conf login_content): inventory hostname, this host's Splunk roles, and admin username/password. All three default to true when unset, which is convenient for a lab VM you can reach only from your laptop. Set them false when the UI is reachable from a wider network (typical AWS) so credentials are not printed on the login form.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_loginpage_print_hostname: false
  splunk_loginpage_print_userpw: false
  splunk_loginpage_print_roles: false
```

#### Share splunk.secret across nodes

`splunk_defaults.splunk_secret_share`

Splunk encrypts passwords with splunk.secret. Sharing that file across Enterprise (splunk) and/or Universal Forwarder (splunkforwarder) hosts lets encrypted values in conf files decrypt on every node. equal true uses one secret for both install types. Defaults are false (each install generates its own secret). Deploy Splunk to one host first so splunk.secret exists (spa deploy --yes --hosts NAME), then deploy the rest.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_secret_share:
    splunk: true
    splunkforwarder: true
    equal: true
```

#### serverName and default hostname

`splunk_defaults.splunk_set_servername`

Sets Splunk serverName (server.conf) and/or the default host field on events to the inventory hostname. Useful in AWS where the guest hostname is an IP or a generated EC2 name. Does not change the Linux hostname (that is os.set_hostname) and does not print the name on the login form (splunk_defaults.splunk_loginpage_print_hostname).

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_set_servername: true
  splunk_set_default_hostname: true
```

#### Splunk SSL for web, inputs, outputs

`splunk_defaults.splunk_ssl`

TLS for Splunk Web, receiving ports (inputs), and forwarding (outputs). enable turns the endpoint on; own_certs true means you place matching certs under auth/ instead of SPA lab certs. Nested config: extra web.conf / inputs.conf / outputs.conf keys for that endpoint. Cert files must be currently valid, RSA >=2048 or EC >=P-256, SHA-2 signature.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_ssl:
    web:
      enable: true
      own_certs: false
```

#### PolicyKit vs sudo for Splunk

`splunk_defaults.splunk_use_policykit`

When true (the usual default), Splunk systemd units use PolicyKit so the splunk user can start/stop the service. Requires the polkit or policykit-1 package from os. Set false to skip the PolicyKit check and install a sudo rule instead, for images that cannot ship polkit.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_use_policykit: true
```

#### Splunk OS user and group

`splunk_defaults.splunk_user`

Linux account Splunk runs as. Ansible roles default to user and group splunk when these keys are omitted. Set them when the image already has a different account (and usually set os.splunk_user_create / splunk_group_create false so SPA does not try to create it).

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_user: splunk
  splunk_group: splunk
```

#### Splunk version

`splunk_defaults.splunk_version`

Which installer tarball under Software to install. latest means the newest version number found there, not a download from splunk.com. Pin a dotted version such as 10.1.0 when several tarballs are present. Can override per host or per splunk_environments entry.

```yaml
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_version: latest
```

#### Software and baseconfig directories

`splunk_dirs`

Paths to Splunk installer tarballs and Premium Solutions baseconfig apps. Prefer spa init --software-dir (stored in ~/.config/spa/paths.yml and copied into env .spa.yml). These config keys override that only when they are not the built-in relative defaults such as ../Software.

```yaml
splunk_dirs:
  splunk_software_dir: ../Software
  splunk_baseconfig_dir: ../Software
```

#### systemd unit extras

`splunk_systemd`

Extra keys passed through to the Splunk systemd unit (LimitNOFILE, environment, and similar). Empty object means role defaults. Only for Linux systemd-managed Splunk, not Windows UF.

```yaml
splunk_systemd: {}
```

| Path | Type | Qualifiers | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `splunk_hosts` | list[object] | required; min_length=1 | Hosts that spa provision and spa deploy act on. Holds no value itself. |
| `splunk_hosts[].cname` | string | optional | DNS alias published for this host. No default. Omit the key to publish none. |
| `splunk_hosts[].custom` | CustomConfig | optional | Ansible connection variables for this host only, such as ansible_user and ansible_port. No default. Omit the key when SPA provisions the host. |
| `splunk_hosts[].idxcluster` | string | optional | Indexer cluster name. Required when roles includes cluster_manager. No default for other roles. Omit the key when the host is not in an indexer cluster. Also associates indexer peers with that cluster. |
| `splunk_hosts[].ip_addr` | string | optional | Guest IPv4 when you assign it yourself. No default. Omit the key to let the provider assign the address. |
| `splunk_hosts[].iter` | object | optional | Generated hostnames from a numeric range. Holds no value itself. |
| `splunk_hosts[].iter.numbers` | string | required; pattern=^\d+\.\.\d+$ | Inclusive numeric range such as 1..3. One host is created per number. Required. |
| `splunk_hosts[].iter.postfix` | string | optional | Text placed after each generated number in the hostname. No default. Omit the key to add nothing after the number. |
| `splunk_hosts[].iter.prefix` | string | optional | Text placed before each generated number in the hostname. No default. Omit the key to add nothing before the number. |
| `splunk_hosts[].list` | list[string] | optional | Hostnames generated from this one entry. No default. Set exactly one of name, list, or iter. |
| `splunk_hosts[].name` | string | optional | Inventory hostname for this one host. No default. Set exactly one of name, list, or iter. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os` | object | optional | Per-host override of `os`: Guest OS settings for this host only. Holds no value itself. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.disable_apparmor` | boolean | optional; default=True | Per-host override of `os.disable_apparmor`: When true, disable AppArmor on Ubuntu and Debian. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.disable_selinux` | boolean | optional; default=True | Per-host override of `os.disable_selinux`: When true, disable SELinux on RHEL and Amazon Linux. Skipped on universal forwarders. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.enable_time_sync_cron` | boolean | optional; default=False | Per-host override of `os.enable_time_sync_cron`: When true, install a cron job that keeps the guest clock in sync. VirtualBox always turns this on. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.packages` | list[string] | optional; default=[] | Per-host override of `os.packages`: Extra packages installed with the guest package manager before Splunk. Java 21 belongs on the search/ITSI host only (java-21-openjdk or openjdk-21-jdk). Do not add it to the global os: block. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.remote_command` | string | optional | Per-host override of `os.remote_command`: Shell command run on the guest before Ansible bootstraps, for an image that lacks Python or acl. No default. Omit the key to skip it. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.set_hostname` | boolean | optional; default=False | Per-host override of `os.set_hostname`: When true, set the guest hostname to its inventory name. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.splunk_group_create` | boolean | optional; default=True | Per-host override of `os.splunk_group_create`: When true, create the Splunk OS group. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.splunk_user_create` | boolean | optional; default=True | Per-host override of `os.splunk_user_create`: When true, create the Splunk OS user. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.ssh_keys` | list[string] | optional; default=[] | Per-host override of `os.ssh_keys`: Public key files on the Ansible controller, appended to the login user's authorized_keys. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.time_zone` | string | optional | Per-host override of `os.time_zone`: IANA time zone set on the guest. Default is the Ansible controller's zone. Omit the key to keep that. |
| `splunk_hosts[].os.update_hosts_file` | boolean | optional; default=True | Per-host override of `os.update_hosts_file`: When true, write every lab host into /etc/hosts. |
| `splunk_hosts[].roles` | list[enum] | required; allowed=cluster_manager\|deployer\|deployment_server\|heavy_forwarder\|indexer\|license_manager\|monitoring_console\|search_head\|universal_forwarder\|universal_forwarder_windows; min_length=1 | Splunk roles for this host. Required. Windows UF is a schema role; VirtualBox Windows images are not a documented lab. |
| `splunk_hosts[].shcluster` | string | optional | Search head cluster name. Required when roles includes deployer. No default for other roles. Omit the key when the host is not in a search head cluster. Also associates search heads with that cluster. |
| `splunk_hosts[].site` | string | optional; pattern=^site\d+$ | Multisite label such as site1. Allowed only for indexer, search_head, or cluster_manager. No default. Omit the key for a single-site lab. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_admin_password` | string | optional | Per-host override of splunk_defaults.splunk_admin_password. No default. Omit the key to inherit the global password. Use an env lookup when you set it. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_architecture` | string | optional; pattern=^(amd64\|x86_64\|arm64)$ | Per-host override of splunk_defaults.splunk_architecture. Tarball CPU suffix for this host only. No default. Omit the key to inherit the global architecture. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_conf` | map[string, map[string, any]] | optional | Per-host override of splunk_defaults.splunk_conf. Extra conf stanzas for this host only. No default. Omit the key to inherit the global stanzas. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_env` | string | optional | Environment name from splunk_environments. No default. Omit the key when the config has one environment. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_fips` | boolean | optional | Per-host override of splunk_defaults.splunk_fips. When true, install this host in FIPS mode. No default. Omit the key to inherit the global FIPS setting. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_license_file` | string | optional | Per-host override of splunk_defaults.splunk_license_file. No default. Omit the key to inherit the global license file. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_outputs` | string | optional | Reserved grouping of which indexers receive this host's data. Not applied; forwarders still send to every indexer. No default. Omit the key. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_search_peers` | string | optional | Reserved grouping of search peers for this host. Not applied. No default. Omit the key. |
| `splunk_hosts[].splunk_version` | string | optional; pattern=^(latest\|\d+(\.\d+)*)$ | Per-host override of splunk_defaults.splunk_version. Installer version for this host only. No default. Omit the key to inherit the global version. |
| `splunk_hosts[].terraform` | object | optional | Per-host override of `terraform`: Terraform settings for this host only. Holds no value itself. |

Omit the key to keep that. spa config set writes an end-of-line comment with the image name and description when AWS can describe the id. Find a current Red Hat image with spa aws --region eu-central-1 --latest-ami --os rhel, or list matches with spa aws amis list --region eu-central-1 --os rhel. ubuntu, amazon_linux, and debian use the same --os form. |

| `splunk_hosts[].terraform.aws.key_name` | string | optional; default='aws_key' | Per-host override of `terraform.aws.key_name`: EC2 key pair name. |
| `splunk_hosts[].terraform.aws.region` | string | optional; default='eu-central-1' | Per-host override of `terraform.aws.region`: AWS region Terraform uses. |

### Snippets

#### Host identity and roles

`splunk_hosts[].name`

The host list spa provision and spa deploy use. Each entry is one host (name), an explicit list of names, or an iter range (prefix + 1..N + postfix). roles is required (cluster_manager, indexer, search_head, deployer, universal_forwarder, universal_forwarder_windows, heavy_forwarder, license_manager, and so on). Cluster managers must set idxcluster; deployers must set shcluster. site is only for indexer, search_head, or cluster_manager. Other catalog settings can override per host under the same entry.

```yaml
splunk_hosts:
  - name: idx1
    roles: [indexer]
```

#### splunk_outputs grouping

`splunk_hosts[].splunk_outputs`

Documented on hosts for a future grouping of which indexers receive data.

```yaml
# Not applied cluster-wide yet. Do not rely on splunk_outputs in config.
```

## Apps

| Path | Type | Qualifiers | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `splunk_app_deployment` | object | optional | Install and removal of add-ons during deploy. Holds no value itself. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.apps` | list[map[string, any]] | optional | App entries to install or remove. Each entry is a map of name, source, and either a Splunkbase id or a local path. No default. Omit the key to deploy no apps. List of apps. Required per entry: name. splunkbase also needs app_id. local needs path when the folder name is not the app name. Normal apps need target_roles. Optional version (latest or dotted), state (installed or absent), deployment_target (auto or direct), serverclass, target_path, and cluster/serverclass filter lists. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.backup_apps_before_update` | Annotated | optional; default=False | When true, back up the existing app directory before an update. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.cache_downloads` | Annotated | optional; default=True | When true, keep the downloaded archive after it is extracted. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.deploymentclient_check` | boolean | optional; default=True | When true, run splunk btool deploymentclient to see which hosts are deployment clients. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.host_specific_apps` | list[map[string, any]] | optional | Reserved. Not applied by deploy. No default. Omit the key. Use target_roles and filters instead. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.local_app_repo_path` | string | optional | Folder of local apps. Default is the apps directory from spa init. Omit the key to keep that. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.splunkbase_password` | string | optional | Splunkbase password for app downloads. No default. Omit the key when every app is local. Use an env lookup when you set it. Use lookup('env', 'SPLUNKBASE_PASSWORD'). Never a literal password in YAML or chat. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.splunkbase_username` | string | optional | Splunkbase user for app downloads. No default. Omit the key when every app is local. Use an env lookup when you set it. Use lookup('env', 'SPLUNKBASE_USERNAME'). Report only whether the env var is set, never the value. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.target_download` | Annotated | optional; default=False | When true, each target downloads the app from Splunkbase. |
| `splunk_app_deployment.update_mode` | enum | optional; default='merge'; allowed=clean\|merge | merge keeps extra files such as local/; clean deletes the old app first. |
| `splunk_apps` | object | optional | Saving rendered baseconfig apps back into the lab. Holds no value itself. |
| `splunk_apps.splunk_save_baseconfig_apps` | boolean | optional; default=False | When true, copy rendered baseconfig apps into the lab. |
| `splunk_apps.splunk_save_baseconfig_apps_dir` | string | optional; default='saved_base_config_apps' | Lab folder that receives saved baseconfig apps. |
| `splunk_apps.splunk_save_serverclass` | boolean | optional; default=False | When true, also save the deployment-server serverclass. |

### Snippets

#### Splunk app deployment

`splunk_app_deployment`

Install or remove normal Splunk apps during deploy from Splunkbase (the default source, plus numeric app_id) or from an extracted local folder (source local plus path under apps_dir). Each apps[] entry needs name and target_roles (which Splunk roles receive it). SPA then picks the target_path: SHC deployer, cluster manager, deployment server, or the host etc/apps. Optional version (latest or dotted), state (installed or absent), update_mode, deployment_target, and serverclass filters. Same name may appear twice with different target_roles (see splunk_app_deployment.apps[].customizations). Credentials must be lookups, never literals.

```yaml
splunk_app_deployment:
  splunkbase_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'SPLUNKBASE_USERNAME') }}"
  splunkbase_password: "{{ lookup('env', 'SPLUNKBASE_PASSWORD') }}"
  apps:
    - name: Splunk_TA_nix
      app_id: 833
      target_roles: [search_head, indexer]
```

#### Splunk IT Service Intelligence

`splunk_app_deployment.apps[].app_id`

Install ITSI as a premium app (premium_app: itsi, Splunkbase app_id 1841). Do not set target_roles. Put Java 21 (not 22+) on the search/ITSI host os.packages (splunk_hosts[].os, java-21-openjdk or Ubuntu openjdk-21-jdk), not in the global os: block. Pair Enterprise plus ITSI license files and a license_manager role. Optional itsi_index_home_path, itsi_index_cold_path, itsi_notification_disable, and shc_rolling_restart (SHC only). CIM, MLTK, Scientific Python, and viz apps in the lab file are normal splunk_app_deployment entries (target_roles), not premium_app. For a full lab copy or merge examples/single_node_itsi.yml; that file is not a spa init --example topology.

```yaml
splunk_hosts:
  - name: sh1
    roles: [search_head]
    os:
      packages: [java-21-openjdk]
splunk_defaults:
  splunk_license_file:
    - Splunk_Enterprise.lic
    - Splunk_ITSI.lic
splunk_app_deployment:
  splunkbase_username: "{{ lookup('env', 'SPLUNKBASE_USERNAME') }}"
  splunkbase_password: "{{ lookup('env', 'SPLUNKBASE_PASSWORD') }}"
  apps:
    - name: Splunk IT Service Intelligence
      source: splunkbase
      app_id: 1841
      premium_app: itsi
```

#### ITSI single-app content pack

`splunk_app_deployment.apps[].content_pack_api`

One ITSI content pack that is its own app folder or archive, not the Content Library. itsi_content_pack true; top-level name is the on-disk pack folder (for example DA-ITSI-CP-CUST-ATLAS-AWS-EBS). Omit content_pack_apps, install_all_apps, and content_pack_install. Optional top-level content_pack_api and customizations. Requires a sibling premium_app: itsi with the same state.

```yaml
splunk_app_deployment:
  apps:
    - name: DA-ITSI-CP-CUST-ATLAS-AWS-EBS
      source: splunkbase
      app_id: 7294
      itsi_content_pack: true
      content_pack_api:
        install_all: true
        enabled: true
```

#### ITSI Content Library (multi-app)

`splunk_app_deployment.apps[].content_pack_apps`

Multi-app ITSI content library (DA-ITSI-ContentLibrary). itsi_content_pack true, top-level name is the on-disk library folder, and content_pack_apps lists each pack folder. On each list item: name is the pack folder; content_pack_install true (default) registers the pack via the ITSI API (false extracts files only); content_pack_api sets install_all, enabled (default false), saved_search_action, backfill, resolution, prefix; customizations may set run_playbook_after_restart (SPA playbook after Splunk is up) and force_run_playbook_after_restart. Those keys belong on the item, never on the library entry. Requires a sibling premium_app: itsi with the same state.

```yaml
splunk_app_deployment:
  apps:
    - name: DA-ITSI-ContentLibrary
      source: splunkbase
      app_id: 5391
      itsi_content_pack: true
      content_pack_apps:
        - name: DA-ITSI-CP-monitoring-alerting
          content_pack_install: true
          content_pack_api:
            install_all: true
            enabled: true
            saved_search_action: disable
            backfill: false
            resolution: overwrite
          customizations:
            run_playbook_after_restart: ansible/apps_playbooks/DA-ITSI-CP-monitoring-alerting_configure.yml
            force_run_playbook_after_restart: false
        - name: DA-ITSI-CP-nix
          content_pack_install: true
          content_pack_api:
            enabled: true
          customizations:
            run_playbook_after_restart: ansible/apps_playbooks/DA-ITSI-CP-nix_configure.yml
            force_run_playbook_after_restart: false
```

#### App customizations per role

`splunk_app_deployment.apps[].customizations.remove`

After deploy, remove files from the app, write local/ conf (local_configs, same shape as splunk_conf), or run a playbook/role (run_playbook, run_playbook_after_restart, run_role). List the same app twice with different target_roles to vary customizations per role. Guide: docs/apps.md#customize-an-app.

```yaml
splunk_app_deployment:
  apps:
    - name: Splunk_TA_nix
      source: splunkbase
      app_id: 833
      target_roles: [search_head]
      customizations:
        remove: [default/indexes.conf]
    - name: Splunk_TA_nix
      source: splunkbase
      app_id: 833
      target_roles: [indexer]
      customizations:
        remove: [default/inputs.conf]
```

#### Premium app discriminator

`splunk_app_deployment.apps[].premium_app`

Premium apps use premium_app on the apps[] entry instead of target_roles. SPA deploys by product role (search heads, cluster manager, license manager, deployer). When both an SHC and a standalone search head exist (or more than one standalone SH), set exactly one of hosts_whitelist (standalone SH names) or shc_whitelist (names from splunk_shclusters). ALLOWED_PREMIUM_APPS is currently only itsi.

```yaml
# premium_app: itsi is the only allowed value. See splunk_app_deployment.apps[].app_id.
# Do not set premium_app: es.
```

#### Save rendered PS baseconfig apps

`splunk_apps`

After deploy, copy the rendered Premium Solutions (org_*) apps and optional serverclass back to the env (default saved_base_config_apps/) so you can inspect or reuse them. Does not install extra Splunkbase apps; that is splunk_app_deployment.

```yaml
splunk_apps:
  splunk_save_baseconfig_apps: true
```
